text: [3:486.1 - 3:486.4] Reserved. 10 (2) [3:486.5] Compare—adjudicative (quasi-judicial) administrative proceedings: An adjudicative administrative proceeding that is the functional equivalent of a lawsuit—i.e., commenced by filing a complaint, governed by rules similar to a judicial proceeding and capable of resulting in a damages award—is deemed a “suit” under insurance policies that do not define the term. Because the undefined term is ambiguous, and the insured reasonably would expect such proceedings to be covered, the insurer owes a duty to defend and indemnify. [Ameron Int'l Corp. v. Insurance Co. of State of Penn. (2010) 50 C4th 1370, 1386, 118 CR3d 95, 107—proceeding before U.S. Dept. of Interior Board of Contract Appeals to resolve government demands against insured parties, commenced by filing of “complaint,” involved 22 days of trial, numerous witnesses and substantial evidence] d. [3:487] Ins.C. § 533 as bar to coverage? Section 533 bars coverage for injury claims arising from the insured's “wilful” (intentional) discrimination against employees (see ¶ 3:105 ff.).
